concepts.def: Opening section presenting the first subject in the tonic and the second subject usually in the dominant (or relative major for minor keys).
Middle section that transforms thematic material through modulation, fragmentation, sequence and contrapuntal techniques.
Final section restating both subjects in the tonic key, resolving the tonal tension of the exposition.
Opening melodic idea, typically in the tonic key with rhythmic and motivic character that drives the movement.
Contrasting theme, usually in the dominant (major mode) or relative major (minor mode); often more lyrical.
Concluding section after the recapitulation that reinforces the tonic and brings closure; may be extensive in late Beethoven.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Appraising — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In sonata form, in what key does the second subject normally appear in the exposition of a piece in a major key?
options: Tonic
Dominant
Subdominant
Relative minor

mcqs.q: Which composer is credited with significantly expanding the coda in sonata-form movements?
options: Mozart
Haydn
Beethoven
Schubert

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
It is always C major.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
A long melody with no breaks.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
All notes are raised by a semitone.
A long melody with no breaks.
It has only five notes.

mcqs.q: What is a balanced antecedent-consequent phrase?
options: Two phrases of equal length where the first sounds open (question) and the second resolves (answer).
A long melody with no breaks.
Any two phrases of similar style.
It has only five notes.
